messages:
maria: Heads-up — getting a bunch of customer reports about mid-response truncation and 502s from the edge for hosted API since ~20:12 UTC. Appears across us-west and eu regions. Sample trace id: trace-9f3a. Customer reproduction attached below.

alex: Noted. Any commonalities? model, streaming vs non-streaming, auth method?

maria: Mostly streaming calls (chat/generate) with token auth. I see spike in upstream RSTs in the gateway logs around the time token rotation job ran.

jordan: Can you paste a minimal curl we can run to repro quickly?

maria: Sure — example request (sanitized):

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"stream test","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream
```

alex: Looking at the edge logs I see repeated `HTTP/2 RST_STREAM` from upstream with code 2 (refused_stream) and 502 returned to client. Also a short burst of TLS handshake retransmits at the same time.

sre-bot: [ALERT] edge-gateway-502-rate > 5/min across us-west-2 eu-west-1. Graphs: https://metrics.company/alerts/1725008888

eng-oncall: Quick triage checklist:
- confirm auth key rotation windows (maria: when did rotation run?)
- check upstream pool exhaustion (envoy h2 concurrent streams)
- TLS session cache churn (last deploy changed backend TLS settings?)

maria: Rotation job started 20:11:30 UTC, rotated a subset of keys and pushed new jwks. We did a canary, but looks like some tenants hit the new keys while others still hitting old ones (key overlap period).

alex: That overlap can cause auth proxy retries if it rejects then backend does fallback causing connection churn. I'm seeing many 502s where the auth-proxy responded 502 after upstream refused streams. Example snippet from edge log:

```
[2024-04-01T20:12:05Z] GET /v1/chat/stream 502 trace-9f3a upstream_rst: RST_STREAM code=0x2
[2024-04-01T20:12:05Z] auth-proxy: jwt verification failed: kid not found
[2024-04-01T20:12:05Z] envoy: connection reset by peer (upstream)
```
jordan: Repro attempt: hit the curl repeatedly ~200 req/s from us-west — I see same early-close after ~450ms on streaming responses.

eng-oncall: Mitigation steps to try now:
- pause rotation rollback (if possible) or pin gateway to previous jwks set
- bump edge idle/keepalive timeouts temporarily to reduce TLS churn
- increase h2 max_concurrent_streams on upstreams by +50% for a short window

maria: Rolled back the rotation canary and pushed previous jwks at 20:18 UTC. Also toggled keepalive from 30s->90s on a subset of upstreams.

alex: After rollback I'm seeing 502s drop to background rate. Confirming: us-west 502 spike window 20:12–20:18. Post-rollback 20:19 onwards 502s down.

maria: Customer confirm: their stream resumed and no further truncation after 20:20.

jordan: Good. Next steps for follow-up:
- full postmortem on rotation rollout process (ensure no half-signed jwks states)
- add a canary circuit in auth-proxy to return 429 vs hard 502 when kid unknown to avoid upstream resets
- add automated smoke tests exercising streaming endpoints during rotation window

eng-oncall: I'll open an incident doc and assign owners. Also will add temporary alert that correlates jwks rotations + edge 502 spikes.

maria: Thanks all — will collect logs and customer repro bundle and attach to the incident.

alex: One small script we used to reproduce the early-choke (in case useful):
```
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"stream test","stream":true}' \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream &
done
wait
```

maria: Closing thread — workaround applied, customers patched. Will track postmortem and controls. :white_check_mark:
